COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
FA No. 5 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for 
the appellants.
2. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned 
counsel for the respondent.
3. The respondent no. 1/plaintiff Ashish 
Mohan Aggarwal filed a suit being OS No. 
134 of 2018 for specific performance 
against respondent no. 2 Mahesh Kumar 
Prajapati (now deceased) and defendant 
no. 2 never put appearance before the 
Trial Court and Trial Court passed an order 
to proceed ex-parte, and, ultimately 
decreed the suit filed by the respondent/ 
plaintiff ex-parte on 23.08.2019. During 
the pendency of the suit, defendant 
Mahesh Kumar Prajapati (now deceased) 
executed a registered will in favour of the 
appellants herein on 07.08.2019. 
Thereafter on 10.10.2019, the 
defendant/respondent Mukesh Kumar 
Prajapati (now deceased) filed an 
application under Order 9 Rule 13 of CPC 
for recalling the ex-parte judgment and 
decree dated 23.08.2019 which was 
dismissed on 01.08.2024 against which an 
appeal bearing AO No. 418 of 2024 was 
filed wherein statement was made by the 
plaintiffs that they will not proceed with 
the execution. During this period, Ashish 
Mohan Aggarwal filed another suit bearing 
suit no. 22 of 2022 challenging the sale 
deed executed by respondent Mukesh 
Kumar Prajapati (now deceased) in favour 
of the appellants herein wherein the  appellants who were defendants in the 
said suit filed their written statements on 
30.07.2022. Simultaneously, respondent/ 
plaintiff initiated execution proceedings by 
way of Execution Case No. 3 of 2020 
wherein on 03.10.2024 the appellant 
herein also impleaded as judgment debtor. 
Subsequent thereto AO No. 418 of 2024 
was dismissed on 25.09.2025.
4. Now, the present appellants herein 
who were arrayed as judgment debtor in 
the execution proceedings preferred 
instant appeal against ex-parte judgment
and decree dated 23.08.2019 passed in 
O.S.No. 134 of 2018.
5. As per the office report, there is a 
delay of 793 days and while computing 
this period, the covid period was also 
excluded.
6. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned 
counsel who appears for the 
respondent/plaintiff submits that the delay 
in preferring the instant appeal is not bona 
fide since the appellant got knowledge 
about ex-parte judgment and decree 
dated 23.08.2019, in the year 2022 when 
O.S. No. 22 of 2022 was filed wherein 
appellants herein filed written statement
on 30.07.2022. Apart from this he submits 
that the appellants herein cannot be 
presumed to be bona fide purchasers in 
terms of Section 3 of Transfer of Property 
Act.
7. In response to this Mr. Piyush Garg 
who appears for the appellants submits 
that on two accounts the delay is liable to 
be condoned, firstly AO No. 418 of 2024 
preferred against the order rejecting 
application under Order 9 Rule 13 CPC was
finally dismissed on 25.09.2025 and 
subsequently the appellants herein first 
time arrayed as judgment debtor in the 
execution proceeding on 03.10.2024, 
therefore, the delay, if any, in preferring  the appeal is only due to lack of 
knowledge of ex-parte judgment and 
decree since cause of action accrues when 
the appellants herein arrayed as judgment 
debtor in execution proceeding on 
03.10.2024.
8. Mr. Singh submits that even 
otherwise as per Limitation Act the delay 
has to be computed from the date of ex￾parte judgment and decree i.e 28.03.2019 
and, as such, there is delay of 1900 days 
in preferring the instant appeal and note 
of the registry is not correct.
9. Let Registry may examine the delay 
since admittedly the instant appeal has 
been preferred against the ex-parte 
judgment and decree dated 23.08.2019 
and place the report before this Court by 
17.12.2025.
10. Put up this matter on 17.12.2025.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
12.12.2025
Parul

08.05.2026 FA No.5 of 2025
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg, learned counsel for the 
appellants. 
2. Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel for 
respondent no.1.
3. The instant First Appeal under Section 96 of 
the Code of Civil Procedure has been preferred on 
behalf of the appellant (third party) against the 
judgment and decree dated 23.08.2019 passed by 
the learned Civil Judge (S.D.), Vikasnagar, District 
Dehradun in O.S. No. 134 of 2018, ‘Sri Ashish 
Mohan Vs. Sri Mahesh Kumar Prajapati’, whereby 
the suit filed by the plaintiff seeking specific 
performance of an alleged agreement to sell has 
been decreed ex parte.
4. There is a delay of 1157 days in filing the 
present appeal. Since there is a delay in preferring 
the First Appeal, the same is accompanied by a 
delay condonation application being IA No. 1 of 
2025.
5. The reasons assigned for the delay are that the
prescribed limitation period for filing the present 
appeal is 90 days from the date of the impugned 
order. The appellants are bona fide purchasers of the 
property in question by virtue of a registered sale 
deed dated 07.08.2019, executed by late Respondent 
No. 2, who was the recorded owner in the revenue 
records. The appellants were unaware of any 
agreement to sell or the pendency of the suit filed by 
Respondent No. 1 against Respondent No. 2. They 
purchased the property in good faith and without 
notice of the prior alleged agreement or pending  litigation. The delay in filing the present appeal 
occurred primarily because the appellants initially 
relied upon the assurances of the LRs of Respondent 
No. 2, who had represented that they were diligently 
pursuing the matter and would protect the interests 
of the appellants. It was only in November 2024, 
upon seeking independent legal advice and 
verifying the case status, that the appellants became 
aware of the lack of diligence and possible collusion 
on the part of the LRs of Respondent No. 2 with 
Respondent No. 1. Furthermore, the appellants 
faced considerable difficulty in obtaining certified 
copies of the judgment, decree, and plaint, as the 
records had been summoned before the Hon’ble 
High Court in connection with another matter, i.e., 
A.O. No. 418 of 2024. Despite repeated efforts and 
filing of applications, the necessary documents 
could be obtained only on 02.01.2025.
6. It is further contented that thus, the delay is 
neither intentional nor attributable to negligence, but 
has occurred solely due to the circumstances stated 
hereinabove. The impugned judgment and decree 
directly affect the rights of the appellants, and if the 
delay is not condoned, the appellants shall suffer 
irreparable loss and injury. The appellants have 
acted bona fide and have shown sufficient cause for 
condonation of delay in filing the present third-party 
appeal.
7. The aforesaid contentions were opposed by 
the learned counsel for respondent no. 1 by filing 
objections, inter alia, contending that no plausible or 
satisfactory explanation has been furnished by the 
appellant, who was admittedly not a party to the 
original suit. After an inordinate delay of more than 
2116 days, no third party can be permitted to 
challenge the judgment merely on the basis of some 
agreement allegedly executed between such 
defendant and the appellants. A third party can, at  best, step into the shoes of its predecessor-in-interest 
and cannot claim any rights superior to or 
independent of those of its vendor. The appellants 
were negligent in pursuing their alleged rights and, 
therefore, cannot be allowed to derive any benefit 
from their own inaction. No proper, plausible, or 
satisfactory cause has been shown by the appellants, 
who are complete strangers to the original 
proceedings. No sufficient cause, much less any 
legally sustainable ground, has been disclosed in the 
delay condonation application or in the affidavit 
filed in support thereof. 
8. In view of the facts and circumstances of the 
case, and considering that the present appeal is a 
third-party appeal preferred along with an 
application seeking leave to appeal, and further that 
the impugned judgment is likely to entail civil 
consequences upon the appellant and that a lis ought 
to be decided on merits rather than being thrown out 
on technicalities and accordingly, purely in the 
interest of justice, the delay in filing the appeal is 
hereby condoned, subject to payment of costs of Rs. 
5,000/-, which shall be deposited by the appellant in 
the High Court Bar Advocate Association Welfare 
Fund within a period of two weeks. Delay 
condonation application (IA No. 1 of 2025) 
accordingly stands allowed.
9. List on 29.05.2026. 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) 
 08.05.2026

FA No.5 of 2025
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the 
appellants.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the 
respondents.
The present appeal is preferred by 
third party along with the Leave to Appeal 
Application.
In the Leave to Appeal Application, it 
has been stated that the appellants are bona 
fide purchasers for value and were
completely unaware of any of such 
agreement in favour of the plaintiff/ 
respondent no.1. The sale deed was 
executed by respondent no. 2 in favour of 
the appellant on 07.08.2019 prior to the 
judgment dated 23.08.2019 passed in O.S.
No. 134 of 2018.
It is further contended that the present 
appeal is a third party appeal. The 
appellants are most necessary and proper
party. The respondent no.2 has already filed 
an execution application as against the 
appellant as well and serious rights of the 
appellants are involved in the matter in 
question.
Per contra, learned counsel for the 
respondents would contend that the 
appellant was well aware about the 
registered agreement to sale in favour of the 
plaintiff/respondent which amounts to 
public notice and they have got the sale deed 
executed in their favour and they cannot be 
termed as bona fide purchaser.
In reply, Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for 
the appellants would reply on the judgment  of Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of H. 
Anjanappa and others vs. A Prabhakar and 
others reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 183 
and drew the attention of this Court to para 
43 viii thereof and has contended that the 
Leave to Appeal is to be granted to persons 
though not parties to the proceedings who 
would be bound by the decree or judgment 
in that proceeding.
In view of the contentions raised by the 
learned counsel for the parties and in view of 
the settled position of law on the subject, the 
Leave to Appeal Application is hereby 
allowed.
The applicant is permitted to prefer the 
appeal against the impugned judgment and 
order dated 23.08.2019. Since the valuable 
rights of the parties have to be adjudicated, 
hence admit the appeal. 
Summon the Trial Court Record.
List this case on 31.07.2026.
Since the appeal has been admitted, 
hence the effect and operation of the 
impugned judgment and order dated 
23.08.2019 shall remain stayed till the next 
date of listing. 
 (Siddhartha Sah, J.) 
 30.05.2026
Ravi
